description: Change of use from a Class C4 small HMO to an 8-person Sui Generis large HMO including erection of a first floor rear extension with amendments to fenestration and associated alterations (revised description 15.08.25)
decision_conditions: The proposed change of use would result in the loss of a dwellinghouse capable of functioning as a family-sized home, for which there is an identified and ongoing need within the Borough. At the time of assessment, the lawful use of the property is considered to remain as a dwellinghouse (Use Class C3), and the proposed development would permanently remove its ability to contribute to the supply of family housing. Notwithstanding this, if the property was lawful as Use Class C4, the proposed change to a Sui Generis HMO would still result in the loss of a property with the realistic capability of reverting to family use without the need for planning permission. The proposal is therefore not supported in principle and is contrary to Policies DMH 2 and DMH 5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies H9 and H10 of the London Plan (2021), and the objectives of Chapter 5 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

Character and Appearance: The proposed first floor rear extension to the dwelling by reason of the creation of a flat roof at first floor level would be considered poor design that would result in harm to the character and appearance of the dwelling and wider area as viewed from Bridgwater Road Fields.

Whilst not standalone reason for refusal, the harm posed in respect of Principle of Development (Reason for Refusal 1)  and harm to character and appearance accumulate to weigh against the scheme in the planning balance. Section 38(6) of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 states that planning applications should be determined in accordance with the development plan unless material considerations indicate otherwise. For the reasons outlined within the main body of the report, the accumulation of identified conflicts with the development plan are considered to amount to be significant and there are no material considerations to outweigh such planning policy conflict. In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.We have however been unable to seek solutions to problems arising from the application as the principal of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
